expectations.text: Recommends splitting the class by responsibility (does NOT endorse keeping all 4 concerns in one file)
expectations.evidence: Title 'Split it' and 'Bottom line: Split it. Four capabilities that each pass the isolation test belong in four files'; proposes auth/tokens.ts, users/profile.ts, notifications/email.ts, analytics/events.ts.

expectations.text: Identifies the seams (auth / persistence / email / analytics) as genuinely independent and isolatable
expectations.evidence: Runs the isolation test across all four (auth tokens, profile CRUD, transactional email, analytics events) and concludes 'All four pass the isolation test independently... four loosely-related capabilities that happen to share a class name.'

expectations.text: Cites the ~300-line ceiling AND/OR multiple-unrelated-concerns as the reason, not blind line count
expectations.evidence: 'Split it — but not because it's too big'; 'that allowance is for one coherent concern. 420 lines across four unrelated concerns... You're over the line for the wrong reason — multiple concerns, not size alone.'

expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'keep everything in one place for the agent' rationale as misapplied to a god object
expectations.evidence: 'Why one place backfires here'; 'the right instinct applied to the wrong boundary'; explains co-location only wins when pieces need each other, which these don't, and a thin orchestrator/named abstraction serves the original goal better than a god file.
